newsitem.title: UK: Syria cuts Souedie crude five cents, no Light deal.
newsitem.headline: Syria cuts Souedie crude five cents, no Light deal.

text.p: Syria's state oil company Sytrol has agreed a five-cent cut in the price of its heavy Souedie crude for March but is still talking to customers about Light barrels, traders said on Friday.
"That's going to be the final price," said a term contract holder referring to market talk that Souedie had been fixed at Dated Brent -$4.80 a barrel from -$4.75 a barrel in February.
Traders said the modest reduction reflected a seasonal improvement in margins for Souedie crude, which has a heavy bitumen yield.
But term customers were still holding out for an improvement on Sytrol's latest offer of Dated Brent -50 cents for Light crude, down from -27 cents in February.
"There has been talk of one lifter accepting -50 cents but with 10 or 11 others still refusing you can't call that an agreement," said one.
Most were still holding out for a discount of around 55/60 cents to Dated Brent, they said.
